name: claude-code-self-tools
description: Small Claude Code plugins that let a session act on itself: compact or clear its conversation, reload its plugins, reconnect an MCP server, read its context window, check its own tools, wake itself later, turn on Remote Control under a title, set its prompt bar color, exit or restart, switch to another conversation, run a command with a secret pasted at the machine that it never sees, make sure Chrome runs for Claude in Chrome, keep the machine's plugins current, read its own desktop on Windows, and read its machine's plugin settings and change the few on a fixed list; and a skill for running several sessions as a hierarchy. Install only the ones you want.

plugins.name: self-compact
plugins.description: Compacts the conversation once the turn ends, at the break between two pieces of work, then resumes on its own.

plugins.name: self-clear
plugins.description: Clears the conversation once the turn ends, only when its work is complete or its context is contaminated, and starts the next piece from a handoff it writes.

plugins.name: self-reload
plugins.description: Reloads the session's plugins once the turn ends, as /reload-plugins does, then resumes on its own.

plugins.name: self-mcp
plugins.description: Reconnects an MCP server that broke (one by name, or all) once the turn ends, as /mcp reconnect does, then resumes on its own.

plugins.name: self-context
plugins.description: Reads how full the context window is, and whether auto-compact is on, to decide whether to compact at a break.

plugins.name: self-check
plugins.description: Checks that the session's own tools answer: a nonce echoed through Bash and PowerShell as the model calls them, the room the session env leaves a Bash command, and the MCP servers listed (exercised only through probes you name). Quietly again at resume, saying only what failed. Dedupes Bash's session env after each session start, against Git Bash's 8,186-character cut.

plugins.name: self-wake
plugins.description: Wakes the session some minutes (or seconds) after the turn ends with a note it sends itself, to check back on slow work.

plugins.name: self-remote-control
plugins.description: Reports on the session's Remote Control, connects it under a title, and renames the session. After a login change it reconnects Remote Control and resumes a turn the change cut off. It runs /remote-control only while the session is not connected.

plugins.name: self-color
plugins.description: Sets the session's prompt bar color once the turn ends, as /color does, to mark its role so sessions are told apart at a glance; default resets it.

plugins.name: self-exit
plugins.description: Ends the session once the turn ends, as /exit does, with a stated reason recorded in its transcript for whoever resumes it; it refuses while a session cron, a background job or a subagent would make /exit ask, saying how to stop each.

plugins.name: self-restart
plugins.description: Restarts the session on Windows once the turn ends: a new window, or the pane's slot, resumes the same conversation once the old process has exited, then resumes work on its own.

plugins.name: self-switch
plugins.description: Switches the terminal to another conversation on Windows once the turn ends, for your own use: only when that conversation is open nowhere on this machine and nothing runs under this session; in place, in the pane's slot, or in a new window. It refuses where the coordinator runs switches. Its launch_sessions tool opens a list of sessions where placement.json's grid puts them.

plugins.name: self-secret
plugins.description: Runs a command with a secret the session never sees: you paste it into a form on 127.0.0.1 in your browser, it is checked before anything runs, handed to that one command in an environment variable, and masked in everything the command prints; a hold keeps it for later commands. The tool answers with the exact command line and runs nothing itself.

plugins.name: self-chrome
plugins.description: Makes sure Chrome runs for Claude in Chrome: looks for your Chrome, starts it when it isn't running (on the profile you name, else on the one profile whose Google account has the email of Claude Code's account; the last session restored; and --silent-debugger-extension-api only when you opt in), and reconnects Claude in Chrome once the turn ends. It never quits or restarts Chrome.

plugins.name: self-update
plugins.description: Keeps the plugins this machine already has from the marketplaces you name current, with Claude Code's own claude plugin commands, one look at a time, and reloads each session behind an update at its next idle moment. Off until you name a marketplace. Windows only.

plugins.name: self-desktop
plugins.description: Reads the session's own machine's desktop on Windows, read only: lists the windows a person could see (a title only for Windows Terminal windows and the session's own), reads the session's own terminal window and the text showing in its own pane, whoever wrote it (never from a console shared by a program that is not the session's own), and captures a classic console window of the session's own to a local PNG; a picture of a Windows Terminal window isn't built. It never clicks, types, focuses, moves or closes anything. Off until you turn it on.

plugins.name: self-settings
plugins.description: Reads this machine's plugin settings as the /config menu shows them (a sensitive field's value never read, a value that looks like a secret never shown), and changes only the options on a fixed list, each plugin's update check and self-compact's compact reminder, through Claude Code's own /config writer. Every other option is the owner's, in /config by hand.

plugins.name: self-hierarchy
plugins.description: A skill, not a mod: how several sessions on one machine run as a hierarchy (an owner, a coordinator, a merger, lanes, and builder and reviewer subagents), and how the self tools keep each session healthy.
